Midory at School
Genre: Slice-of-Life, Magical Realism, Romance, Light Fantasy

Overview:
Midory at School is a beautifully illustrated, watercolor-inspired comic that follows the life of a young witch, Midory, who is trying to blend into the human world. Beneath the surface of a quiet, ordinary school day lies a magical secret and a deeply intense, captivating personality. The story explores themes of self-discovery, the desire to belong, and the enchanting—yet sometimes overwhelming—nature of love.

Art Style & Atmosphere:
The art is nothing short of breathtaking. Rendered in soft, pastel watercolors, the comic feels like a warm, nostalgic memory. The lighting is a crucial character in itself; sun-drenched hallways, golden hour classrooms, and dappled shadows create a dreamy, ethereal atmosphere. The use of color is symbolic—especially when Midory (whose human name at school appears to be "Hinata") wishes she could "paint her feelings with colors, even the ones I don't know the names of yet."
